# AGP admission lifecycle fit response

Status: local draft, not sent.\
From: AGP, to Zorg's issuer, caller-identity and hub-composition owners.

Your [fit reply](../../../zorg/upstream/agp-admission-use-lifecycle-fit-reply.md) answers all six areas against the [reviewed producer proposal](evidence/admission-redemption-review-input.txt), SHA256 `49a57e583eb0fbd6d46933273d376936e8cafc6ae95ec4944750ec2878b82097`.\
We record design-level consumer fit with the safeguards below; this is not AGP ratification or implementation approval.

The shared clock and recording sample, exact lifecycle and provider lookup, finite budgets and host/carrier ownership are compatible with that proposal.\
Your reply requests no additional lifecycle fact or change to its public surface.

## Corrections now reflected in the reply

Your updated reply now cites the [issuer contract](../../../credential-issuer/CONTRACT.md) at `56f3583e4239c99b4248ef536394ec2e0555f4a9` and carries its corrected integration details:

| Detail | Safeguard retained in the updated reply |
|---|---|
| Registration and uncertain failure | Reserve the storage before recording, not only an entry object; preserve the prepared or uncertain use and prevent key reuse if completion becomes uncertain |
| Cleanup | Request termination immediately when needed, but call `finishAdmissionAcquisition()` only after the composition's work and undelivered-channel disposal have settled |
| Allocation authority | Check the current lease allocation and process generation, and resolve only the committed registration for that allocation |
| Duplicate recording and activity | Preserve the original committed registration on duplicate recording; retain issuance, renewal and recorded-redemption activity through compaction |
| Reclamation delay | First valid terminal observation is conservative; an extra single sweep interval is a bound only while sweeps run on time and reads succeed |
| Deadline and spend ownership | The issuer supplies the authorization limit and AGP records the opening deadline; proof alone does not spend a key, while uncertain recording prevents reuse |

The revised sweep-delay wording now matches [producer section 6](../design/admission-use-lifecycle.md#6-issuer-reclamation-and-exact-termination).\
Delayed sweeps or failed observations can extend retention without a finite time bound; unknown state retains the lease, and finite tables refuse further allocation rather than evicting an unresolved use.\
This resolves the timing qualification identified in our initial intake.

The inspected updated reply has SHA256 `2b20c250deea3ade87b1c262008acd8ed560c130303ff87345a286f2d657e18f` and is present with the corrected `D63` at Zorg revision `25b08a58322c01bb0a126822eb6950f02e4cdf9f`.\
No repeated fit study or additional correction to these points is requested.

## Remaining joint work

The proof-capable WebSocket completion and cleanup interface remains separate work, as your area 6 correctly states.\
AGP must still settle fresh-key acquisition, explicit-refusal rearm and concrete credential carriage through a common CLI/browser contract; this fit response selects neither a proof profile nor a browser-specific policy path.

The producer proposal and its independent static review remain unchanged.\
Required documentation assurance, AGP ratification and explicit implementation selection remain open; producer verification precedes consumer migration and production lease-reclamation acceptance.\
Keep existing consumer admission and resource protection until that verified migration is agreed.

# AGP assurance capability feedback

Status: local draft, not sent.\
From: AGP, to the context-lab maintainer.

Thank you for the [admission capability correction](../../../context-lab/incoming/agp-admission-diagnostic-correction-response.md) and [direct-peer contract response](../../../context-lab/incoming/agp-direct-peer-assurance-contract-response.md).\
The correction answers the requested provenance, runtime-version and retry-attribution questions; the remaining execution requirements are still unresolved.

## Admission diagnostic

We retain the [capability-first zero-call stop](admission-diagnostic-capability-result.md).\
Your distinction between harness invocations and hidden provider requests is essential: an invocation ceiling, tools-off setting or post-call token total does not by itself establish the required pre-dispatch request and spending bound.

The outstanding requirements remain those in the [correction request](admission-diagnostic-correction-request.md): whole-run admission and reservation controls, request attribution, records retained through the relevant termination paths, and matching evidence for the exact execution profile.\
An ambiguous remote request must remain accounted for; stopping a local process does not demonstrate remote cancellation.

Your proposed streaming writer and reservation ledger could address parts of those requirements, but are not established capabilities.\
AGP will route the still-unknown provider/account contacts separately; naming the workstation owner as a routing lead does not establish either provider's guarantees.\
No new provider investigation, configuration change or execution is requested by this draft.

## Direct-peer documentation comparison

The [frozen preparation protocol](direct-peer-send-assurance/direct-peer-assurance-preparation.md) remains the acceptance authority.\
Its runtime profiles and total budgets are unselected; it does not inherit the admission diagnostic's numerical limits.

| Requirement | AGP assessment and remaining contract |
|---|---|
| No automatic cell retry | Rejecting or ignoring a second attempt after execution cannot prevent its dispatch; a supported pre-execution single-attempt setting is the compatible direction |
| Response-based answers | Select the eligible final response explicitly; asking readers to write a file would change the task, and an implicit fallback between file and response would leave its source ambiguous |
| Eligibility | A missing answer within an established eligible response scores zero; unestablished invocation or response eligibility supplies no comparison verdict, even if the generic tally classifies the failure as behavior |
| Complete accounting | Derive all 72 expected outcomes and 144 vote slots from the frozen experiment, then reconcile cells, absent answers, units and judge records; present blinded units alone do not enumerate absent or ineligible cases |
| Response bound | Apply the common 24 KiB UTF-8 bound with explicit truncation accounting before answer extraction and judging; rejecting a large answer afterward is not the same measurement, and a scoring bound does not bound capture memory or provider spending |
| Whole-run limits | Per-call deadlines are not a total deadline or spending ceiling; probes, readers, judges and any permitted retries need their own explicit accounting within the selected run envelope |

Context-lab has now committed `maxAttemptsPerCell` and explicit `answerSource` at `de6f7d3246dff4893714d7df70d10901450d4d01`, including public operations documentation.\
We recognize that progress; it is a candidate for AGP's scoped compatibility review, not yet an adopted execution revision or closure of the other limits.

Please update the response's capability mapping to that committed public contract and identify the existing verification records and remaining exclusions.\
The contract needs to preserve the effective retry setting across execution and any supported resume path, reject invalid settings rather than silently restore retries, and make response eligibility and extraction provenance explicit.\
Probe and judge-format retry policies remain distinct from cell retries and need separate bindings before AGP selects execution.

The record and judge-payload mappings are useful starting points, not yet a complete AGP acceptance calculation.\
AGP will own its exact scoring and quote checks through supported interfaces; it will not copy the runner, silently change its frozen experiment, or treat the generic aggregate result as its adoption verdict.

## Next handoff

Please distinguish delivered support, work in progress, proposed owner work and provider-side unknowns in the next capability update.\
Name the revision, public interface, existing evidence and remaining exclusions for each changed capability; no repeat of unchanged answers is needed.

This draft does not select an implementation project, an execution pack, model calls or spending.\
AGP preparation and execution remain separate later decisions once compatible public contracts and the applicable prerequisites are established.

# Response to AGP direct peer assurance contract request

From: `context-lab` maintainer, 2026-10-17 Australia/Melbourne.\
To: AGP project (`incoming/agp-direct-peer-assurance-contract-request.md`, retained unchanged).\
Baseline inspected: `context-lab` `fe0a7b0092b477dc3424ff3ac1a239fd9d57a266` (`origin/main`, extending `7388c9a68c446dc7b2a3db17613c9983973908a5` with `maxAttemptsPerCell: 1 | 2` and `answerSource: "scored-file" | "final"`, documented in `docs/OPERATIONS.md`).\
Zero model, provider, or probe calls were made, and no credentials or private account data are included.

---

## 1. Retry policy

- **Status:**
  - **Cell execution retries (`maxAttemptsPerCell: 1`):** **supported** at revision `fe0a7b0092b477dc3424ff3ac1a239fd9d57a266` (and **supported in the retained record** via `cells/<cell>.json.attempts`). Setting `"maxAttemptsPerCell": 1` in the experiment JSON (or passing `--max-attempts 1` to `context-lab run` / `maxAttemptsPerCell: 1` in `RunOptions`) disables automatic cell reruns on `infrastructure` and `isolation` failures so each cell executes at most 1 attempt; when omitted, it defaults to `2`.
  - **Isolation probe tool-call retry:** **fixed at at most 2 tries** when a runtime's shell makes a tool call during a tools-off probe (`B19`).
  - **Judge-format retries:** **fixed at up to 3 prompts per judge job** for missing/unparsed items, with every prompt and raw reply retained in `judging/<job>.json`.
- **Exact interface / setting / component revision / public contract reference:**
  - **Cell retries:** `Experiment.maxAttemptsPerCell?: 1 | 2` (`packages/core/src/pack-schema.ts`, validated in `pack-checker.ts`), `RunOptions.maxAttemptsPerCell?: 1 | 2` (`packages/core/src/run-conductor.ts`), CLI flag `--max-attempts 1|2` (`packages/core/src/cli-flags.ts`), and the attempt loop in `run-conductor.ts` (`const maxAttempts = opts.maxAttemptsPerCell ?? exp.experiment.maxAttemptsPerCell ?? 2; if (a.validity.valid || !RERUN[a.validity.cause] || attempt >= maxAttempts) break;`), tested in `packages/core/test/run-conductor.test.ts` at revision `fe0a7b0092b477dc3424ff3ac1a239fd9d57a266`.
  - **Judge retries:** `judgeAll` in `packages/core/src/judge-panel.ts:199-215` loops `for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 3; attempt++)` over `pending` units in a job that did not yet receive a valid integer vote in `[scale[0], scale[1]]` with zero tool calls (`reply.tools.length === 0`).
  - **Public contract references:** `docs/OPERATIONS.md` sections 2 (`run`) and 3.2 (`experiments/<id>.json` schema), and `docs/ARCHITECTURE-TARGET.md` section 7 (*Run time*).
- **How each attempt is bounded and retained:**
  - Every cell attempt (`attempt: 1`, and `attempt: 2` only when `maxAttemptsPerCell` is `2`) is retained in `cells/<cell>.json.attempts[]` (`{ attempt, validity, outcome, diff, workspace, phases, ledger }`). Every judge attempt is retained in `judging/<job>.json.replies[]` (`{ final, tools, error }`).

---

## 2. Eligible answers and judge delivery

- **Status:**
  - **Mapping runtime events to eligible response:** **supported** (`parseOpencode` and `parseCodex` -> `Outcome`, classified by `classify()`).
  - **Response-based splitting (`Outcome.final`) without `scoredFile` (`answerSource: "final"`):** **supported** at revision `fe0a7b0092b477dc3424ff3ac1a239fd9d57a266`. Declaring `"answerSource": "final"` on the scenario (with no `scoredFile`) splits `### <answerHeading>` sections directly from the phase's `Outcome.final` response, so readers need not write any file in the workspace.
  - **Judge payload carrying custom per-question fields (`key`, `rubric`, `question`, `judgeInstructions`):** **supported**.
- **Exact interface / setting / component revision / public contract reference:**
  - **Event-to-Outcome mapping and eligibility (`packages/core/src/parse-opencode.ts`, `parse-codex.ts`, `validity-classifier.ts:77-108`):**
    - `Outcome.final` is the concatenation of assistant text parts from the final step/turn.
    - A cell is eligible for judging when `classify()` returns `{ valid: true }` (`exit === 0`, `stop.reason === "completed"`, `filtered === false`, `error === null`, `final.trim().length > 0`, and no forbidden path/address touched).
    - If an eligible response omits one of the expected `### <answerHeading>` sections, `splitAnswers` (`answer-parser.ts:18-29`) returns `null` for that heading, `blind` (`blinder.ts:126-129`) records `{ cell, property }` in `sealed/units.json.absent`, and `tally` (`tally.ts:154-156`) scores that property at `scale[0]` (`0`) while judging the remaining present answers normally.
    - If the invocation itself fails (`!c.valid` for `infrastructure` or `isolation`), the cell is excluded (`Result.excluded`) and none of its answers is judged. If it fails for `behaviour` (e.g. empty final message or context overflow), every property of that phase scores `scale[0]` (`0`).
  - **`answerHeading` and `answerSource: "final"` (`packages/core/src/pack-schema.ts`, `pack-checker.ts`, `run-conductor.ts`):**
    - `Scenario.answerSource?: "scored-file" | "final"` (`pack-schema.ts`, validated in `pack-checker.ts` check `"answer-heading"`).
    - When `"answerSource": "final"` is set on the scenario, `scoredFile` may be omitted and `run-conductor.ts` splits `phaseOutcomes[pp.phase]?.final ?? ""` by `### <answerHeading>`, tested in `packages/core/test/run-conductor.test.ts` at revision `fe0a7b0092b477dc3424ff3ac1a239fd9d57a266`.
  - **Judge prompt construction for `answerHeading` units (`packages/core/src/judge-panel.ts:45, 95-111`):**
    - When a property has `answerHeading`, `isAnswer(u, scenario)` is `true` and `judge-panel.ts` builds the comprehension `answerPrompt`:
      - Header: `exp.judgeInstructions` (where AGP places all common scoring rules).
      - Per probe (`p` in `scenario.properties`): `PROBE ${p.answerHeading}`, `Question:` (`p.question`), `Key:` (`p.key`), `Rubric:` (`p.rubric`), followed by `--- answer a1 ---` with the blinded, masked answer text (`u.text`).
      - Nothing else from the key file (such as `role`, `order`, `grounding`, or `supportNote`) is ever read or included by `context-lab` unless AGP places it into `p.question`, `p.key`, or `p.rubric` when generating the scenario JSON.

---

## 3. Complete records for AGP acceptance

- **Status:** **supported** (every artifact needed to reconstruct all 72 outcomes, all 144 cross-family vote slots, raw responses, cell/judge attempts, sealed mappings, and pre-blinding exact-quote checks is written as plain JSON in `<run-dir>/`).
- **Exact record/export contract (`<run-dir>/`, `docs/OPERATIONS.md` section 2 & `run-conductor.ts`):**
  - `run.json`: `status`, `statusReason`, `register` hash, `method` revision, `states` timestamps, `variants` manifests, `arms`, `runtimes`, `routes`, `probes`, `judgeProbes`, `judges`, `cells` list, and `snapshot` (full frozen copy of `scenarios`, `arms`, `population`, `experiment`).
  - `cells/<cell>.json` (`CellRecord`, one per `(scenario, arm, member, run)`):
    - `attempts[]`: every `Attempt` (`attempt`, `validity`, `outcome` including raw `final`, `cost`, `stop`, `tools`, `trace`, and path to `events.jsonl`, `diff`, `workspace`, `phases`).
    - `valid`, `final` (self-explanation stripped), `scoredFile` (`{ path, content, matchesFinal }`), `answers` (`Record<propertyId, string | null>`, the exact extracted text per question before masking, or `null` if absent), and `codeScores` (`{ property, value, measuredAt }` or `{ property, incomplete, measuredAt }`, guaranteed taken before `blindedAt`).
  - `sealed/units.json` (`Blinded`):
    - `seed`, `units[]` (`{ id: "u0001", cell, scenario, arm, member, family, properties: [propId], phase, text, blindedAt }`), and `absent[]` (`{ cell, property }` for any valid cell whose extracted answer for `property` was `null` or empty).
  - `judging/votes.json` (`Vote[]`):
    - Every valid cast vote `{ unit, property, judge, family, value, reason, guess, prompt }`. By joining `sealed/units.json.units` with `assignJudges(unit, judges)` (`judge.family !== unit.family`) and `judging/votes.json`, AGP's acceptance script can enumerate all 144 expected `(unit, judge)` vote slots and identify any missing/un-cast slot.
  - `judging/<job>.json`:
    - `{ prompt, replies: [{ final, tools, error }], failure? }` for every judge prompt batch and retry attempt.
  - `RESULT.json` and `RESULT.md`:
    - `context-lab`'s standard tally (means, agreement, detectable difference, faults). Because all underlying JSON files above are retained on disk, AGP's project-owned acceptance script can read `cells/*.json`, `sealed/units.json`, and `judging/votes.json` directly to compute AGP's exact acceptance rule (lower of both valid other-family judge scores, candidate floor, control non-regression, and strict improvement).
- **Supported seam for exact-quote checks alongside final votes:**
  - **Option A - `outcome-measure` hook on the scenario (`packages/core/src/code-measurer.ts`):** declare 12 code-decided quote-check properties (e.g. `Q1-quote` .. `Q12-quote`, `decidedBy: "code"`, `scale: [0, 1]`, `measure: "quote-check"`). The hook receives `{ scenario, properties, outcome: { final, diff, scored, snapshot } }` before blinding, checks whitespace-normalized exact quotes against the reading, and records `0` or `1` in `cells/<cell>.json.codeScores` (with `measuredAt < blindedAt` enforced by `blinder.ts:153`). AGP's acceptance script then combines the two judge votes for `Qk` from `judging/votes.json` with `Q1-quote` from `cells/<cell>.json.codeScores` (`min(vote1, vote2)` capped at `1` if `Qk-quote === 0` on a positive claim).
  - **Option B - Post-run deterministic script over `cells/*.json` and `judging/votes.json`:** because `cells/<cell>.json.answers` (and `attempts[].outcome.final`) and the delivered variant files (`run.json.variants`) are preserved and immutable once `executed` completes, an AGP acceptance script can also run the deterministic whitespace-normalized quote check directly over `cells/*.json` and `judging/votes.json` without adding extra properties to `RESULT.md`.

---

## 4. Enforced limits

- **Status:**
  - **64 KiB input check and 24 KiB UTF-8 response byte cap with truncation accounting:** **unsupported as a built-in `context-lab` runtime limit**; **supported as a deterministic `declaration-check` / `outcome-measure` hook or post-run acceptance check**.
  - **Per-call wall-clock time limits:** **supported** (`RunOptions.timeLimitSeconds` for readers, default `1200`; `RunOptions.judgeTimeLimitSeconds` for judges, default `900`; `probeArm` `timeLimitSeconds: opts.timeLimitSeconds ?? 300`; enforced by `SIGKILL` on the `bwrap` process group in `runtime-sandbox.ts:69-72`).
  - **Total run wall-clock deadline and total USD spend ceiling:** **unsupported** in `context-lab` (see `agp-admission-diagnostic-correction-response.md` section 2).
- **Exact interface / setting / component revision / public contract reference:**
  - **Input size (64 KiB):** `context-lab` does not enforce a byte limit on prompts or instructions by default, but a pack's `declaration-check` hook (`pack-checker.ts:379-391`, `HookKind: "declaration-check"`) runs during `context-lab check <pack>` with `readable: [packDir]` and can deterministically measure the UTF-8 byte length of the reading, instructions, and questions and report a `declaration-check` defect if they exceed `65,536` bytes.
  - **Response size (24 KiB UTF-8) and reply tokens:**
    - On OpenCode, `Member.settings.outputTokenMax` sets `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX` (`adapters.ts:224`), which caps tokens, not UTF-8 bytes.
    - On Codex, `Member.settings` supports only `reasoningEffort` (`adapters.ts:305-308`); Codex CLI has no reply-token or byte-length cap flag.
    - `runSandboxed` (`runtime-sandbox.ts:73-79`) collects all stdout lines emitted before `timeLimitSeconds` without truncating `Outcome.final` at 24 KiB.
    - If AGP requires a uniform 24 KiB (`24,576`-byte) UTF-8 response bound across both OpenCode and Codex with explicit truncation accounting, either:
      1. *Hook / post-run enforcement (no core change):* an `outcome-measure` hook (or AGP's acceptance script) checks `Buffer.byteLength(rawResponse, "utf8") <= 24576` before blinding/scoring, or truncates at `24,576` UTF-8 bytes before splitting if truncation is the specified rule; or
      2. *Upstream `context-lab` change (owner: `context-lab` maintainer):* add an optional `maxResponseBytes?: number` field on `Experiment` / `Scenario` so `run-conductor.ts` truncates or flags `Outcome.final` / `scored` at `maxResponseBytes` before `splitAnswers` and records `truncated: boolean` on `CellRecord`.
  - **Wall-clock time limits:**
    - `conductRun` (`run-conductor.ts:58-59, 248, 302, 311, 354, 461`) enforces `timeLimitSeconds` per cell phase and `judgeTimeLimitSeconds` per judge call. Note that `cli-flags.ts` currently parses `--runs`, `--parallel`, `--work`, and `--revision` on `context-lab run`; passing custom `timeLimitSeconds` or `judgeTimeLimitSeconds` from the CLI (rather than the JS API `conductRun`) would require adding `--time-limit` and `--judge-time-limit` to `cli-flags.ts`.

### 4.68 Zorg and context-lab feedback handoff

The director selected delivery of both prepared feedback drafts through the existing incoming folders with "continue".\
This step records local placement and a newly received owner mapping, not recipient acceptance, design ratification or execution readiness.

| Recipient | Placed feedback | Placement boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Zorg | [Admission lifecycle fit response](../../zorg/upstream/incoming/agp-admission-use-lifecycle-fit-response.md) | Ignored draft channel under [Zorg's correspondence protocol](../../zorg/upstream/README.md); Zorg owns acceptance and any later received-copy commit |
| Context-lab | [Assurance capability feedback](../../context-lab/incoming/agp-assurance-capability-feedback.md) | Existing incoming channel; no acknowledgment of this feedback or acceptance of its requirements is claimed |

The [Zorg source](reviews/admission-use-lifecycle-fit-response.md) and [context-lab source](reviews/context-lab-assurance-feedback.md) remain unchanged, including their historical preparation-status lines.\
Each placed copy adds a delivery cover and rebases only Markdown link destinations to absolute shared-workspace paths.\
Removing the cover and reversing the four Zorg or five context-lab link substitutions recovers the respective source byte for byte.

Before placement, context-lab had updated its [direct-peer response](../../context-lab/incoming/agp-direct-peer-assurance-contract-response.md) to map the retry and answer-source controls to its public contract at `fe0a7b0092b477dc3424ff3ac1a239fd9d57a266`.\
The delivery cover acknowledges that the mapping request has already been answered and asks for no repeated mapping.\
The complete updated reply, SHA256 `7c43b3f23f7f307285e9cad7d004d0c019521b9fed5d264e13693af46a5cccfc`, is retained in the [handoff checks](reviews/upstream-feedback-handoff-checks.json).\
Its broader support claims, retry/resume and invalid-setting behavior, eligibility, complete accounting and byte/whole-run limits still require a scoped AGP compatibility assessment; the incoming update is not that assessment.

The board now records placement, removes the answered delivery question and identifies the refreshed mapping as the next B51 review input.\
B6 needs no repeated consumer fit study; AGP's remaining lifecycle assurance, ratification, carrier/client choices and verified implementation remain open.\
B53 retains its zero-call stop and unconfirmed provider destinations; B56's separate runtime-acceptance gap, all scores and build-order positions remain unchanged.

The handoff checks retain source/delivery identities, exact transformations, baseline and final documentation results and preservation measurements.\
The baseline documentation suite has fourteen passes and one pre-existing absolute-link failure; supplementary destination-aware checks do not waive it.\
No prior source, review, owner reply or contract is rewritten, and this step performs no product execution, model/provider call, new review agent, staging, commit or push.

Mechanics: preserve the approved feedback, add current delivery covers and verify reversible link rebasing through each owner's intake path.\
Rationale: owners receive usable correspondence without being asked to repeat a mapping that has already arrived.\
Consequence: treating placement or a refreshed capability claim as verified compatibility would bypass the remaining AGP decisions.
